name: AI Driver
description: The rival field: how many AI cars line up on the grid, where they start, and the steering policy that takes each one around world.track_circuit's gates. It exists because a circuit with one car on it is a time trial, and the genre's loop is 'overtake, place'. It drives through the same car model movement.vehicle_basic publishes for the player's own body, issuing throttle and steer rather than positions, so a rival obeys the same grip and drag and can be out-braked into a corner. It applies utility.rubber_band_ai's pace multipliers to the sheet it drives with (top speed and acceleration), never to position, and reports the running order — lap, then gate, then distance to the next gate — as standings, because it is the only component that knows every body in the race. It owns grid placement and the field; it does not own what a lap is (world.track_circuit scores the rivals' gates exactly as it scores the player's), how a car feels (movement.vehicle_tuning), or the handicap (utility.rubber_band_ai). Contact between cars is soft separation only, announced as an impact so a screen shake can hear it; damage belongs to combat.ram_damage_model.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: rivalCount
inputs.description: AI cars on the grid. Zero is a time trial and still a valid build.

inputs.name: paceFraction
inputs.description: Rival top speed and acceleration as a fraction of the player's effective tune sheet, before any rubber band. Below 1 so a clean lap beats the field on merit; the band works from here.

inputs.name: lookAheadFraction
inputs.description: How early a rival starts blending its aim toward the gate after next, as a fraction of the gate radius scaled distance. Higher takes smoother lines; too high clips gates and voids laps.

inputs.name: gridSpacing
inputs.description: World units between grid slots laid back from the start line.

inputs.name: contactRadius
inputs.description: Distance under which two cars push apart. Zero disables contact entirely.

outputs.name: racers
outputs.description: Every rival body: id, position, heading, velocity and the pace multiplier in force. world.track_circuit reads it to score their gates; a presentation layer reads it to draw them.

outputs.name: standings
outputs.description: Racer ids in running order, the player included as 'player'. Lap first, then gates crossed, then distance to the next gate.

outputs.name: playerPosition
outputs.description: The player's 1-based place in the field. What a position readout shows.

provenance: Asked for after the racing pack booted with one car on the circuit: the genre's own loop reads 'launch, corner, overtake, place' and nothing in the catalogue owned a second car, a grid, or a running order. utility.rubber_band_ai and persistence.ghost_replay both assume rivals exist and neither drives one; world.track_circuit disowns grid placement and standings in its own description.
